newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian police round up Jihad activists.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian police round up Jihad activists.

text.p: Palestinian police have rounded up activists of an Islamist movement which Israel said sent two suicide bombers on failed missions to kill Jews in Gaza, Palestinians said on Wednesday.

Islamic Jihad (Holy Struggle) sources said police detained about 30 of their activists during overnight raids. It disavowed the two bombings, charging instead that Israel staged them on Tuesday to divert attention from its Jewish settlement policy.
"There are arrests to find out those who are conspiring against the Palestinian Authority," Palestinian Attorney-General Khaled al-Kidra told Reuters.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem has triggered 13 days of clashes, has conditioned further peace moves with the Palestinians on an end to violence.
The blasts on Tuesday killed the two Palestinians whom Israel said were bombers. No Israelis died in the explosions 15 minutes apart near Jewish settlements.
The Palestinian Authority said witnesses had testified that an object thrown from an Israeli military jeep was responsible for one of the explosions.

"The Islamic Jihad in Palestine declares from the Gaza Strip as it did abroad through its leader Dr Ramadan Shallah that it has nothing to do with the operations that occurred yesterday," Sheikh Abdallah al-Shami told a news conference in Gaza.
"The military operations which took place yesterday were planned by the Israeli Shin Bet secret service and the Mossad to serve a political goal," he said, referring to Israeli secret services.

Only a few hundred Palestinians paid condolences at the family homes of Abdallah al-Madhoun, 19, and Anwar al-Shabrawi, 20, who were buried on Wednesday. Many Palestinians believe the two were set up by Israeli secret service agents.
Shami said he did not know whether the two were members or supporters of Islamic Jihad. But he insisted that Israeli secret service agents were involved in the bombings.
He said Israel's government had recently authorised the Shin Bet to resume work in Palestinian self-rule areas.

Islamic Jihad activists say Israeli agents have in the past intercepted the group's secret messages and tampered with them to set up activists before arresting them -- and have staged attacks that would justify action against them.
The Islamic militant mainstream Hamas group has also distanced itself from the blasts and accused Israel of staging them.

Both groups have in the past taken responsibility for suicide attacks that have killed scores of Israelis, issuing leaflets and making anonymous telephone calls to local media and international news organisation.
